answers.answer: Each player chooses a color and places that color's Player ID upright in its stand in front of them. Give each player the Voting set with their color on the backs, remove cards targeting colors not in the game, and keep their own Ambush. Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center with values hidden; the deck remains face down beside the play area.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘puts its Player ID card upright in its plastic stand’; ‘Remove cards targeting colors that are not playing’; ‘Deal four Gold Bar cards face down to the center.’

answers.answer: There is no player-by-player turn order. A player may change their chosen face-down card until cards are revealed. Once everyone has chosen, all choices are revealed simultaneously.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘There is no individual turn order.’ Vote: ‘You may change your chosen card until cards are revealed’ and ‘reveal all choices simultaneously.’

answers.answer: No four-vote majority is needed. Red is the sole Target because Red has the most votes (three); the Target is whoever receives the most votes, regardless of whether that count is a majority of all votes.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘The player receiving the most votes is the Target.’

answers.answer: Red and Blue are both Targets because they tie for the most votes, and, with neither protected by a successful Ambush, both are eliminated. A player may satisfy the voting requirement and survive by voting for either tied Target.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘If several players tie for the most votes, all of them are Targets’; with tied Targets, ‘voting for any one of them satisfies the voting requirement.’

answers.answer: No. Green is eliminated: Green did not vote for the sole Target, Blue. Receiving no votes does not protect Green. No Ambush exception applies.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘Every other player who did not vote for any Target is also eliminated,’ subject to the successful Ambush exception.

answers.answer: Red's Ambush does not count as a vote. Yellow's vote for Red and Pink's vote for Yellow are one vote each, so Red and Yellow tie for the most votes and are both Targets. Red's Ambush succeeds; Red survives and may eliminate Yellow, the player who voted for Red. Pink survives because Pink voted for tied Target Yellow. Red and Pink remain.
answers.evidence: The three-player example says Red plays Ambush, Yellow votes Red, Pink votes Yellow; ‘Red and Yellow tie at one vote each and are both Targets’; Red can retaliate only against Yellow; Pink survives, leaving Red and Pink.

answers.answer: No. The successful ambusher chooses one player who voted for them to eliminate, even if four players voted for them. They may not choose someone who voted for another color instead.
answers.evidence: Ambush: ‘chooses one of the players who voted for them’; ‘They cannot choose an arbitrary player or someone who voted for a different Target.’

answers.answer: The player eliminates themselves. An Ambush works only when its player is a Target; if not a Target, it fails and that player self-eliminates.
answers.evidence: Ambush: ‘An Ambush played by someone who is not a Target fails: that player eliminates themselves.’

answers.answer: No gold is awarded yet. With four survivors, the round continues with another Conspire and vote among those surviving players; only survivors participate in subsequent votes.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Three or more | Continue with another conspiracy and vote among survivors.’

answers.answer: The sole survivor collects all four central Gold Bar cards. They are four cards, not four points; each card is worth 3, 4, or 5 points, and their values are hidden until revealed for scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘One | That survivor collects all four central Gold Bars.’ Components: ‘receiving one bar means receiving one card whose value is 3, 4, or 5 points.’

answers.answer: They resolve a Final Showdown for the central Gold Bars. Each takes a set of Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go cards; they may discuss intentions and a bargain, then each chooses one card, places it face down, and they reveal simultaneously when both are ready.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: ‘each takes a set containing Share, Steal, and Grab One & Go’; each chooses one face down; ‘When both are ready, reveal both choices simultaneously.’

answers.answer: Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Players who participated in that final vote receive no consolation bar, including those eliminated by that vote. Leave the four central bars for the next round and add no new bars.
answers.evidence: None-survivor resolution: ‘Each player who was not participating in the final vote receives one Gold Bar from the deck. Leave the four central bars for the next round; add no new bars.’

answers.answer: Each finalist receives two Gold Bar cards.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Share against Share: ‘You get 2; opponent gets 2.’

answers.answer: The Steal player receives all four central Gold Bar cards; the Share player receives none.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Share against Steal: Share player gets 0; Steal player gets 4.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Steal player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Steal: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: The Grab One & Go player receives one central bar, and the Share player receives the other three.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown table: Grab One & Go against Share: ‘You get 1; opponent gets 3’; Grab One & Go always gives its player exactly one bar.

answers.answer: Each finalist takes one central bar, leaving two in the center. If play continues, add just two new bars to the center, restoring the pool to four.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: ‘each receives one and the other two bars remain central’; ‘Leave the remaining two in the center and add just two new bars for the next round.’

answers.answer: Neither finalist receives gold. Every other player receives one Gold Bar card from the deck. Leave all four central bars for the next round and add no new gold to the central pool.
answers.evidence: Final Showdown: ‘If both choose Steal, neither finalist receives gold’; ‘give every other player one Gold Bar from the deck’; ‘Leave all four central bars for the next round.’

answers.answer: Check for victory at the end of the round, after Gold Bars are awarded. With 6–9 players, the threshold is at least 25 points; with 10–12, it is at least 24. If multiple players qualify with different totals, the player with the highest point total wins.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘Check for victory at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded’; thresholds are 25 for 6–9 and 24 for 10–12; ‘the highest point total wins.’

answers.answer: The booklet's instruction is that tied highest qualifying totals conduct another Final Showdown, repeating Showdowns as necessary until one player has the highest total. If a normal round has no winner, everyone returns for the next round: stand all Player ID cards upright.
answers.evidence: Scoring: tied qualifying players ‘conduct another Final Showdown’ and ‘Repeat these Showdowns as necessary’; Turn Structure: ‘If there is no winner, everyone returns: stand all Player ID cards upright.’

answers.answer: Before every vote, players discuss or signal their intended targets for roughly a minute and a half at most. Any communication method is allowed, including secretly (such as whispering), texting, or showing a Voting card. When it is time to vote, the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.
answers.evidence: Conspire: ‘for roughly a minute and a half at most’; ‘Any method of communication is allowed, openly or secretly,’ including whispering, showing a Voting card, and texting; ‘the game owner asks everyone for their final decisions.’

answers.answer: To cast an ordinary vote, choose the Voting card matching the target's visible ID color and place it face down. If you want to defend yourself against being targeted, play your own Ambush card instead.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘Each surviving player places one Voting card face down’; target with the card matching the player's visible ID color; ‘To defend yourself against being the target, play your Ambush card instead.’

answers.answer: Knock down the Player ID cards of eliminated players. Leave surviving players' IDs upright; they are eligible for the next vote.
answers.evidence: Vote: ‘Knock down eliminated players' ID cards. Leave surviving IDs upright for the next vote.’

answers.answer: If nobody wins after the round's rewards, everyone returns and all Player ID cards are stood upright. Keep central bars left behind and refill the central pool to four bars as needed; do not replace bars explicitly left there. Thus after a full-pot award leaves no bars, deal four new central bars.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: ‘Refill the central pool to four Gold Bars as needed; bars explicitly left behind remain there.’ Player Reference: ‘Keep leftover central bars and refill only to four.’

answers.answer: No. Blue remains a Target because Blue received the most votes; a successful Ambush lets Blue survive and retaliate but does not change who the vote made a Target. Purple does not become the Target on the basis of Blue surviving. Voters for Purple have not voted for a Target (Blue), so they are eliminated, unless independently protected by a successful Ambush. The summary does not give the specific Blue/Purple four-to-three example, but its stated Target and elimination rules support this result.
answers.evidence: Vote: most votes determines the Target and Ambush cards do not count; Ambush: it works only if its player is a Target, protects that Target, and allows one retaliation; elimination requires voting for a Target.

answers.answer: The booklet's tie instruction is to conduct another Final Showdown and repeat Showdowns as necessary until one player has the highest total. The summary says the booklet gives no arrangement or procedure for a Final Showdown involving three or more tied leaders; publisher clarification is needed.
answers.evidence: Scoring: ‘tied players conduct another Final Showdown’ and ‘Repeat these Showdowns as necessary’; unresolved source limitation: ‘It provides no arrangement for three or more players tied.’

answers.answer: Yes, if that outside player ends the end-of-round check with a qualifying total and the single highest point total: the summary says victory is checked after bars are awarded and the highest qualifying total wins. The summary does not expressly discuss this compensation-bar tiebreak scenario, so that application is an inference from its scoring rules. If the player is not at the required threshold, the summary does not support declaring them the winner.
answers.evidence: Scoring: victory is checked ‘at the end of a round, after Gold Bars have been awarded’; players who received bars check accumulated card point values; ‘the highest point total wins.’
